chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has surplus from His sustenance which He grants to whom He wills of His creation. And Allah extends His hands at every dawn for the one who sinned at night, asking, "Will he repent so that I may forgive him?" And He extends His hands at sunset for the one who sinned during the day, asking, "Will he repent so that I may forgive him?"'

key_terms.بَاسِطٌ یَدَیْهِ: Extending His hands (a metaphor for mercy)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about Allah's mercy and timing for forgiveness?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the concept of 'Fudul' (superabundance) in divine sustenance, illustrating Allah's boundless patience by extending the door of repentance specifically at the transitions of night and day. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the immediacy of divine mercy, where the 'stretching of hands' symbolizes an open invitation for sinners to return before the final call of death, reinforcing the hope central to Islamic theology.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his predecessors that the  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “Allah  gives  abundant sustenance to whomsoever He desires. Similarly the mercy of    Allah is spread far and wide for the sinners day and night waiting for the person to repent and be forgiven. The mercy of Allah waits at sunset for the people who committed sins during the day to repent and get themselves forgiven.”
